topics.name: Artificial Neural Networks
topics.description: A computational model inspired by the way biological neural networks in the human brain process information.

sub_topics.name: Neurons
sub_topics.description: Basic units of artificial neural networks that process input and produce output.

sub_topics.name: Activation Functions
sub_topics.description: Functions that determine the output of a neuron based on its input.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of linear algebra, calculus, and programming.
common_misconceptions: Neural networks can learn without data
More layers always mean better performance

topics.name: Backpropagation
topics.description: A supervised learning algorithm used for training artificial neural networks by minimizing the error.

sub_topics.name: Loss Function
sub_topics.description: A function that measures the difference between predicted and actual outcomes.

sub_topics.name: Gradient Descent
sub_topics.description: An optimization algorithm used to minimize the loss function during training.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of calculus, linear algebra, and neural networks.
common_misconceptions: Backpropagation is the same as training a neural network.
It only works for feedforward networks.

topics.name: Linear Separation
topics.description: A concept in machine learning where data points can be separated by a linear boundary.

sub_topics.name: Linearly Separable
sub_topics.description: A condition where two classes can be separated by a straight line.

sub_topics.name: Linear Regression
sub_topics.description: A statistical method for modeling the relationship between a dependent variable and one or more independent variables.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of linear algebra and statistics.
common_misconceptions: Linear separation is always possible for any dataset.
Only two-dimensional data can be linearly separated.

topics.name: Training Techniques
topics.description: Methods and strategies used to train machine learning models effectively.

sub_topics.name: Supervised Learning
sub_topics.description: A type of learning where the model is trained on labeled data.

sub_topics.name: Unsupervised Learning
sub_topics.description: A type of learning where the model is trained on unlabeled data.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of machine learning concepts and algorithms.
common_misconceptions: More data always leads to better models
Training and testing data can be mixed
Complex models are always better

topics.name: Neural Networks
topics.description: A collection of algorithms that mimic the operations of a human brain to recognize relationships in data.

sub_topics.name: Deep Learning
sub_topics.description: A subset of machine learning that uses neural networks with many layers.

sub_topics.name: Convolutional Neural Networks
sub_topics.description: A type of neural network particularly effective for image processing.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of linear algebra and calculus, familiarity with programming concepts.
common_misconceptions: Neural networks can learn without data
More layers always mean better performance

topics.name: Regression Analysis
topics.description: A statistical process for estimating the relationships among variables.

sub_topics.name: Linear Regression
sub_topics.description: A method for modeling the relationship between a scalar response and one or more explanatory variables.

sub_topics.name: Logistic Regression
sub_topics.description: A statistical method for predicting binary classes.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of statistics and algebra.
common_misconceptions: Regression implies causation
All relationships are linear
practical_applications: Predicting sales based on advertising spend
Estimating housing prices based on features

topics.name: Classification Techniques
topics.description: Methods used to categorize data into predefined classes.

sub_topics.name: Support Vector Machines
sub_topics.description: A supervised learning model that analyzes data for classification.

sub_topics.name: Decision Trees
sub_topics.description: A model that uses a tree-like graph of decisions and their possible consequences.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of statistics and programming.
common_misconceptions: Classification is only for binary outcomes
More features always improve model performance

topics.name: Model Evaluation
topics.description: Techniques used to assess the performance of machine learning models.

sub_topics.name: Cross-Validation
sub_topics.description: A technique for assessing how the results of a statistical analysis will generalize to an independent data set.

sub_topics.name: Confusion Matrix
sub_topics.description: A table used to describe the performance of a classification model.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of machine learning concepts and statistics.
common_misconceptions: Accuracy is the only metric that matters.
Overfitting is not a concern if the model performs well on training data.
All models should be evaluated the same way.
practical_applications: Comparing different models for a given dataset.
Selecting the best model for deployment.

topics.name: Optimization Algorithms
topics.description: Methods used to adjust the parameters of a model to minimize the loss function.

sub_topics.name: Stochastic Gradient Descent
sub_topics.description: An iterative method for optimizing an objective function.

sub_topics.name: Adam Optimizer
sub_topics.description: An optimization algorithm that computes adaptive learning rates for each parameter.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of calculus and linear algebra, familiarity with machine learning concepts.
common_misconceptions: Optimization is only about finding the minimum.
All optimization algorithms converge at the same rate.
practical_applications: Tuning hyperparameters in machine learning models
